jobs.title: Reporting Clinical Laboratory Scientist (contractor)
jobs.description:
A Rare Opportunity to Shape the Future of Genomics

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

The Prenatal
Reporting Clinical Laboratory Scientist (RCLS) contractor
is responsible for performing high-complexity clinical laboratory data analysis, reviewing and interpreting molecular diagnostic and sequencing results, and ensuring the accuracy, reliability, and timely reporting of patient results in accordance with established laboratory procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

The RCLS independently executes validated bioinformatics pipelines, evaluates analytical results and quality control metrics, troubleshoots, and reviews and releases clinical laboratory reports within established authorization and reporting procedures. For complex or unusual results requiring additional evaluation, the RCLS collaborates with Bioinformatics, the Laboratory Directors, and other appropriate clinical personnel to ensure accurate interpretation and reporting.

In addition to routine clinical reporting responsibilities, the RCLS is expected to demonstrate technical leadership by exercising sound scientific judgment, independently investigating complex analytical issues, providing technical guidance to colleagues, supporting personnel training, and identifying opportunities for continuous process improvement. The RCLS may also participate in additional technical leadership activities and cross-functional initiatives as assigned by laboratory leadership.

The RCLS collaborates closely with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Quality Assurance Management, Genetic Counselors, the Laboratory Directors and other cross-functional teams to support accurate clinical reporting, resolve technical challenges, and maintain efficient laboratory workflows.

The nature of this position requires exceptional attention to detail, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced clinical laboratory environment. The successful candidate must demonstrate initiative, accountability, adaptability, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. This role is a hybrid work arrangement requiring approximately 60% on-site presence at the Union City and/or Menlo Park offices (three days per week on-site and two days per week remote).

Responsibilities

Analysis and Reporting (70%)

Clinical Genomic Data Analysis and Interpretation

Execute established and validated bioinformatics pipelines to process and analyze molecular diagnostic data from patient samples.
Independently review and interpret clinical genomic data, including sequencing results, bioinformatics outputs, and associated quality control metrics, to ensure results meet established quality standards and reporting criteria.
Identify, investigate, and troubleshoot analytical discrepancies, unusual findings, and potential data quality issues, collaborating with Bioinformatics and other appropriate technical teams to resolve complex issues as needed.
Independently manage daily sample analysis priorities, monitor analytical workflows, and proactively communicate technical issues or concerns that may impact reporting accuracy or turnaround times.

Clinical Reporting and Quality Review

Independently review, verify, and release clinical laboratory reports in accordance with established procedures, documented personnel authorization, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Collaborate with other RCLSs, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counselors, Laboratory Directors, and other appropriate clinical personnel to evaluate complex findings, resolve reporting discrepancies, and obtain additional review or approval when necessary.
Ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of clinical reports while managing daily reporting priorities and maintaining established quality standards and turnaround time expectations.
Maintain accurate documentation of analytical reviews, quality assessments, investigations, and reporting decisions in accordance with established laboratory procedures.
Communicate reporting concerns and unresolved issues promptly to appropriate personnel, supporting continuity of reporting operations and timely resolution of sample-specific issues.

Technical Leadership, Quality Assurance, and Operational Support (30%)

Technical Leadership and Training

Demonstrate initiative, accountability, and sound scientific judgment when performing clinical data analysis and reporting responsibilities.
Independently investigate complex analytical discrepancies, troubleshoot technical issues, and identify appropriate solutions or escalation pathways.
Serve as a technical resource for other Reporting CLS personnel by sharing knowledge, providing guidance, and supporting consistent application of established analytical and reporting procedures.
Assist with training, onboarding, and mentoring Reporting CLS personnel and other clinical laboratory staff as appropriate.
Promote technical competency, reporting consistency, and adherence to established laboratory procedures and quality standards.
Proactively identify opportunities to improve reporting accuracy, workflow efficiency, and overall laboratory performance.
Participate in additional technical leadership activities, such as coordinating technical investigations, supporting validation projects, or contributing to workflow improvements, as assigned by laboratory leadership.

Quality Assurance and Regulatory Compliance

Perform and support quality control and quality assurance activities to maintain the accuracy, reliability, and integrity of clinical laboratory testing and reporting.
Ensure compliance with applicable Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), College of American Pathologists (CAP), California state regulations, and established laboratory policies and procedures.
Identify, document, and investigate quality-related issues, including analytical discrepancies, nonconforming results, and deviations from established procedures.
Collaborate with Quality Management and laboratory leadership to support root cause investigations, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
Maintain accurate documentation and records in accordance with established quality management and regulatory requirements.

Process Improvement and Workflow Optimization

Identify and recommend opportunities to optimize analytical workflows, improve reporting accuracy, enhance operational efficiency, and promote cost-effective laboratory practices.
Collaborate with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counselors, and Process Engineering teams to support the development, validation, implementation, and optimization of new or updated laboratory tests, analytical methodologies, and reporting workflows.
Assist with technology transfer and implementation of validated methodologies from Process Engineering into the clinical laboratory.
Support the evaluation and implementation of improvements to laboratory data management and reporting systems.
Maintain and update reporting procedures, technical documentation, and workflow resources to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compatibility with established laboratory processes.
Participate in investigations of recurring analytical or workflow issues and contribute to the development and implementation of appropriate solutions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Operational Support

Collaborate with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counseling, Client Services, Quality Assurance Management, and Process Engineering to investigate and resolve sample-specific and workflow-related issues.
Communicate analytical findings, technical concerns, and recommended solutions clearly and effectively to relevant stakeholders.
Serve as a technical point of contact for cross-functional teams when addressing clinical reporting questions or troubleshooting analytical issues, as appropriate.
Support laboratory leadership with reporting priorities, operational coordination, and project deliverables as needed.
Contribute to cross-functional initiatives that improve laboratory efficiency, reporting reliability, and overall operational performance.

Qualifications

Must possess an active and valid CLS or Clinical Genetic Molecular Biologist Scientist (CGMBS) license issued by the state of California pursuant to Division 2, Chapter 3 of the California Business and Professions Code or to practice medicine, osteopathy or podiatry pursuant to Division 2, Chapter 5 of the California Business and Professions Code appropriate to the specialty they are performing
Bachelor's degree or higher in Biomedical Laboratory Sciences, Clinical Laboratory Science, Molecular Biology, Genetics, or a related scientific discipline, consistent with applicable licensure requirements.
At least one year of clinical laboratory experience or equivalent experience in a high-complexity, high-volume molecular diagnostic clinical laboratory environment.
Working knowledge of molecular biology principles, clinical laboratory testing methodologies, and applicable local, state, and federal laboratory regulations.
Demonstrated experience with sequencing data analysis, including evaluation and interpretation of next-generation sequencing (NGS) results and associated analytical quality control metrics in accordance with validated laboratory procedures.
Demonstrated ability to independently analyze complex laboratory data, investigate discrepancies, and troubleshoot issues affecting test performance or reporting accuracy.
Familiarity with bioinformatics analysis outputs and their application to clinical molecular diagnostic reporting.
Strong computer skills and the ability to effectively use laboratory data management systems and analytical software. Proficiency with commonly used workplace and collaboration tools, including Atlassian Suite, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, and organizational and problem-solving skills, with a commitment to accurate and reliable clinical reporting.
Ability to independently manage reporting responsibilities, prioritize competing demands, and adapt to changing operational needs while maintaining quality and turnaround time expectations.
Demonstrated initiative and accountability in investigating technical issues, identifying solutions, and exercising appropriate judgment regarding consultation and escalation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide technical guidance and collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
Receptiveness to feedback and commitment to continuous learning, professional development, and process improvement.

Benefits And Perks

Working alongside brilliant, kind, passionate and dedicated colleagues, in an empowering environment, toward a global vision, striving for a future in which transformative molecular diagnostics can help millions of patients

Job Summary

Title Lab Technician:

Position Overview

We are seeking an inquisitive and motivated Junior Lab Technician to support our testing and prototyping operations. In this role, you will assist engineering teams with the day-to-day setup, maintenance, debugging, and verification of hardware and software environments. This is a hands-on position ideal for an early-career technician, recent graduate, or self-taught builder passionate about embedded hardware, Linux environments, and robotics or autonomous platforms.

Key Responsibilities

Lab & Bench Setup: Assemble, wire, and configure test benches, sensors, actuators, microcontrollers, and single-board computers (SBCs).

System Testing & Flashing: Flash operating system images and firmware onto embedded devices; assist with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests.

Linux Environment Support: Boot, configure, and maintain Linux-based development machines and edge devices (setting up network interfaces, permissions, and packages).

Autonomous Hardware Support: Mount, calibrate, and verify sensors (e.g., LiDAR, cameras, IMUs, GPS) used across autonomous and robotic test rigs.

Troubleshooting & Diagnostics: Use standard lab equipment (multimeters, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) and software log utilities to isolate hardware, wiring, and communication faults.

Inventory & Safety: Maintain lab equipment inventory, organize test rigs, and enforce lab safety protocols (ESD protection, battery handling, power supplies).

Required & Preferred SkillsCore Qualifications

Associate degree, trade school certification, or equivalent practical experience in Electronics, Robotics, Computer Engineering Technology, or a related field.

Familiarity with basic electronic prototyping, wiring, crimping, and reading basic schematics or pinout diagrams.

Strong organizational skills and the ability to log and document test procedures clearly.

Highly Regarded Skills (Expanded)

Linux Systems & Command-Line Operations

Practical comfort navigating the Linux terminal (e.g., Ubuntu/Debian flavors).

Managing services (systemctl), reading system logs (journalctl, dmesg), and basic shell scripting (bash) for automating repetitive setup routines.

Basic networking configuration (SSH, static IP setup, ping/traceroute, Wi-Fi/Ethernet interfaces) for remote device access.

Embedded Systems & Microcontrollers

Practical experience working with SBCs (Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA Jetson) and microcontroller platforms (ESP32, STM32, Arduino).

Understanding of low-level communication protocols: UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN bus.

Experience with firmware updates, image flashing tools (e.g., balenaEtcher, dd), and serial debugging tools (minicom, screen, PuTTY).

Autonomous & Robotic Platforms

Exposure to the sensor hardware that enables autonomy (cameras, ultrasonic sensors, LiDAR, IMU, wheel encoders).

Basic familiarity with robotics middleware or architectures (e.g., ROS/ROS 2, ArduPilot, PX4) is a significant plus.

Experience troubleshooting physical moving systems, motor controllers, servo actuation, and battery management systems (LiPo/Li-ion safety).

Data Analyst (Mid-Level)

Role Summary

The Data Analyst is an individual contributor who has moved beyond supervised execution and is developing the independence, analytical depth, and stakeholder skills needed to progress to Senior level. They own smaller analytical domains end-to-end, contribute meaningfully to team standards, and begin to proactively surface insights rather than waiting to be directed.

What You'll Do

Analytics & Insight Delivery

Deliver analytical work end-to-end for assigned business areas — from scoping and analysis through to presentation and stakeholder follow-through — with minimal re-direction
Support ad-hoc analysis for internal stakeholders including Marketing, Product, Finance, and Account Management, providing interpretive framing alongside data outputs rather than data retrieval alone
Begin to proactively surface trends, anomalies, and data-driven observations to stakeholders, developing the instinct to flag what matters without being asked
Support A/B test experiments under the guidance of the Senior DA — including data preparation, metric tracking, and results summaries — building toward independent experimental design at Senior level

Google Analytics & Data Collection

Support the Senior DA in GA4 reporting, tracking plan validation, and custom dimension and metric implementation
Develop working knowledge of GA-to-warehouse integration and tagging practices in preparation for owning this domain at Senior level

BI Development & Semantic Layer

Design, build, and maintain Looker dashboards and Explores for assigned business areas, owning deliverables with limited rework
Develop LookML including dimensions, measures, derived tables, and Explore configurations — ensuring all work is documented and consistent with team standards
Contribute to the shared semantic layer by flagging metric definition inconsistencies and proposing resolutions in collaboration with the Senior DA and Analytics Engineering team
Expand self-service analytics for non-technical stakeholders, enabling them to answer their own questions and reducing ad-hoc request volume to the team
Maintain accuracy and consistency of production Explores and dashboards as underlying data warehouse structures evolve

Data Quality & Platform Collaboration

Take ownership of data accuracy for assigned dashboards and analytical outputs — proactively investigating discrepancies and escalating upstream issues to Data Engineering with clear root-cause evidence
Write performant SQL including window functions and CTEs; collaborate with Data Engineers on query optimisation and derived table design
Develop a working understanding of data pipelines feeding owned dashboards sufficient to diagnose freshness and quality issues and communicate resolution timelines to stakeholders
Begin collaborating with Analytics Engineers on LookML architecture and semantic layer requirements for owned areas

Standards & Collaboration

Follow and actively contribute to coding standards, SQL style guides, LookML conventions, documentation requirements, and PR review processes
Participate in code reviews, providing constructive and consistent feedback that builds quality across the team
Support Junior Analysts through paired working and direct feedback, under the guidance of the Senior DA
Partner closely with Senior Analysts, Data Engineers, and business stakeholders; ask clarifying questions early and communicate proactively on blockers and timelines

AI-Augmented Analytics

We believe in having a broad range of talent and backgrounds at U.S. News. We strive to maintain a welcoming and inclusive workplace where everyone is given an opportunity to succeed and contribute to their fullest.

Your Role in Helping Us Shape the Future

As a Data Analyst on our Education team, you will be a guardian of the data integrity that defines our world-renowned rankings. You will work within a specialized, collaborative team to transform raw data into the insights that help millions of students and families make informed life decisions.

Your contributions will follow the academic data cycle:

Data Architecture & Logic: You will spend significant time developing, refining, and executing code to process complex datasets for our signature education rankings. You will eventually contribute to ongoing refinement and validation of ranking methodologies to ensure analytical defensibility and consistency year over year.
Process Optimization & Automation: You will contribute to ongoing efforts to streamline data workflows, including automation of survey universe creation and improvements to production efficiency across ranking calculations and outputs.
Quality Assurance: You will perform rigorous audits of peer-developed code, data inputs and programming outputs, ensuring every data point meets our standards for accuracy.
Anomaly Detection & Validation: You will help enhance processes for identifying outliers, structural shifts, and unexpected model behavior, including exploring automated and AI-assisted methods for anomaly detection and validation.
Collaborative Problem Solving: You will partner with our technical, product and editorial teams to assist with website and guidebook presentation of school rankings and data, methodologies, and editorial content.

Analytical Rigor: A keen eye for detail and the ability to maintain high levels of accuracy while managing large, complex datasets.
Effective Communication: The skill to translate technical data findings into clear, actionable insights for non-technical stakeholders.
A Commitment to Excellence: A proactive approach to identifying data inconsistencies and a dedication to the prestige of the U.S. News brand.

Job Description

This is a Part-Time, Limited Appointment position**

This position is in the Department of Pediatrics, Division of Pediatric Nephrology. The purpose of the position is to support research on the discovery of small molecule modulators of ion transporters/channels important in human diseases, including kidney diseases (kidney stones, kidney failure, hypertension), digestive disorders (diarrhea, constipation, motility disorders), pulmonary diseases (asthma, cystic fibrosis), cardiovascular diseases (hypertension) and others.

Together with the other SRA’s in the lab, the incumbent is expected to perform shared general lab maintenance duties such as defrosting freezers, cleaning hoods, incubators & sinks, organizing supplies inventory, and overall lab maintenance & upkeep. The Prenatal
Reporting Clinical Laboratory Scientist (RCLS) contractor
is responsible for performing high-complexity clinical laboratory data analysis, reviewing and interpreting molecular diagnostic and sequencing results, and ensuring the accuracy, reliability, and timely reporting of patient results in accordance with established laboratory procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

The RCLS independently executes validated bioinformatics pipelines, evaluates analytical results and quality control metrics, troubleshoots, and reviews and releases clinical laboratory reports within established authorization and reporting procedures. For complex or unusual results requiring additional evaluation, the RCLS collaborates with Bioinformatics, the Laboratory Directors, and other appropriate clinical personnel to ensure accurate interpretation and reporting.

In addition to routine clinical reporting responsibilities, the RCLS is expected to demonstrate technical leadership by exercising sound scientific judgment, independently investigating complex analytical issues, providing technical guidance to colleagues, supporting personnel training, and identifying opportunities for continuous process improvement. The RCLS may also participate in additional technical leadership activities and cross-functional initiatives as assigned by laboratory leadership.

The RCLS collaborates closely with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Quality Assurance Management, Genetic Counselors, the Laboratory Directors and other cross-functional teams to support accurate clinical reporting, resolve technical challenges, and maintain efficient laboratory workflows.

The nature of this position requires exceptional attention to detail, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced clinical laboratory environment. The successful candidate must demonstrate initiative, accountability, adaptability, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Analysis and Reporting (70%)

Clinical Genomic Data Analysis and Interpretation

Execute established and validated bioinformatics pipelines to process and analyze molecular diagnostic data from patient samples.
Independently review and interpret clinical genomic data, including sequencing results, bioinformatics outputs, and associated quality control metrics, to ensure results meet established quality standards and reporting criteria.
Identify, investigate, and troubleshoot analytical discrepancies, unusual findings, and potential data quality issues, collaborating with Bioinformatics and other appropriate technical teams to resolve complex issues as needed.

Clinical Reporting and Quality Review

Independently review, verify, and release clinical laboratory reports in accordance with established procedures, documented personnel authorization, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Collaborate with other RCLSs, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counselors, Laboratory Directors, and other appropriate clinical personnel to evaluate complex findings, resolve reporting discrepancies, and obtain additional review or approval when necessary.

Maintain accurate documentation of analytical reviews, quality assessments, investigations, and reporting decisions in accordance with established laboratory procedures.

Technical Leadership and Training

Job Summary

Title Lab Technician:

Position Overview

We are seeking an inquisitive and motivated Junior Lab Technician to support our testing and prototyping operations. In this role, you will assist engineering teams with the day-to-day setup, maintenance, debugging, and verification of hardware and software environments. This is a hands-on position ideal for an early-career technician, recent graduate, or self-taught builder passionate about embedded hardware, Linux environments, and robotics or autonomous platforms.

Key Responsibilities

Lab & Bench Setup: Assemble, wire, and configure test benches, sensors, actuators, microcontrollers, and single-board computers (SBCs).

System Testing & Flashing: Flash operating system images and firmware onto embedded devices; assist with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests.

Linux Environment Support: Boot, configure, and maintain Linux-based development machines and edge devices (setting up network interfaces, permissions, and packages).

Autonomous Hardware Support: Mount, calibrate, and verify sensors (e.g., LiDAR, cameras, IMUs, GPS) used across autonomous and robotic test rigs.

Troubleshooting & Diagnostics: Use standard lab equipment (multimeters, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) and software log utilities to isolate hardware, wiring, and communication faults.

Inventory & Safety: Maintain lab equipment inventory, organize test rigs, and enforce lab safety protocols (ESD protection, battery handling, power supplies).

Required & Preferred SkillsCore Qualifications

Associate degree, trade school certification, or equivalent practical experience in Electronics, Robotics, Computer Engineering Technology, or a related field.

Familiarity with basic electronic prototyping, wiring, crimping, and reading basic schematics or pinout diagrams.

Strong organizational skills and the ability to log and document test procedures clearly.

Highly Regarded Skills (Expanded)

Linux Systems & Command-Line Operations

Practical comfort navigating the Linux terminal (e.g., Ubuntu/Debian flavors).

Managing services (systemctl), reading system logs (journalctl, dmesg), and basic shell scripting (bash) for automating repetitive setup routines.

Basic networking configuration (SSH, static IP setup, ping/traceroute, Wi-Fi/Ethernet interfaces) for remote device access.

Embedded Systems & Microcontrollers

Practical experience working with SBCs (Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA Jetson) and microcontroller platforms (ESP32, STM32, Arduino).

Understanding of low-level communication protocols: UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN bus.

Experience with firmware updates, image flashing tools (e.g., balenaEtcher, dd), and serial debugging tools (minicom, screen, PuTTY).

Autonomous & Robotic Platforms

Exposure to the sensor hardware that enables autonomy (cameras, ultrasonic sensors, LiDAR, IMU, wheel encoders).

Basic familiarity with robotics middleware or architectures (e.g., ROS/ROS 2, ArduPilot, PX4) is a significant plus.

Experience troubleshooting physical moving systems, motor controllers, servo actuation, and battery management systems (LiPo/Li-ion safety).

Data Architecture & Logic: You will spend significant time developing, refining, and executing code to process complex datasets for our signature education rankings. Process Optimization & Automation: You will contribute to ongoing efforts to streamline data workflows, including automation of survey universe creation and improvements to production efficiency across ranking calculations and outputs.

Job Description

This is a Part-Time, Limited Appointment position**

This position is in the Department of Pediatrics, Division of Pediatric Nephrology. The purpose of the position is to support research on the discovery of small molecule modulators of ion transporters/channels important in human diseases, including kidney diseases (kidney stones, kidney failure, hypertension), digestive disorders (diarrhea, constipation, motility disorders), pulmonary diseases (asthma, cystic fibrosis), cardiovascular diseases (hypertension) and others.

Together with the other SRA’s in the lab, the incumbent is expected to perform shared general lab maintenance duties such as defrosting freezers, cleaning hoods, incubators & sinks, organizing supplies inventory, and overall lab maintenance & upkeep. The SRA will attend weekly laboratory meetings unless in direct time conflict with ongoing research/experiments, and will perform other duties as assigned.
